## General info

Code used for creating long-billed hermit song cultural evolution trees and analyzing evolutionary patterns.

## Song segmenting

Songs are now coded as sequences of 5 ms segments with 5 possible states, in four steps. The [full report](https://marce10.github.io/lbh_cultural_evolution_revBayes/source/song_segment_coding_5ms.html) is built from `source/song_segment_coding_5ms.qmd`.

1. **Manual broad sections**: each song is divided into pure tone and trill sections. Consecutive pure tone sections are merged, and trills that differ discretely in rate stay as separate sections
2. **Classify trills**: each whole trill section is fast (F, period < 13 ms) or slow (S, period ≥ 13 ms)
3. **Split into 5 ms segments**: the whole song is split, and trill segments take the state of their section
4. **Classify pure tones**: each tone segment is descending (D, slope < -14 kHz/s), flat (P) or ascending (U, slope ≥ 14 kHz/s), with the slope measured in a 15 ms window

Output files are in `data/processed`:

| Output | Five leks used in the paper (197 recordings, 104 song types) | All leks (322 recordings, 187 song types) |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| Segments | `song_5ms_segments_by_recording.csv` | `song_5ms_segments_by_recording_all_leks.csv` |
| Sequence per song type and year | `song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon.csv` | `song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon_all_leks.csv` |
| One sequence per song type | `song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type.csv` | `song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type_all_leks.csv` |
| FASTA of all recordings | `song_sequences_5ms/all_recordings.fa` | `song_sequences_5ms/all_recordings_all_leks.fa` |
| FASTA files for alignment | `song_sequences_5ms/song_type_sequence/` and `song_sequences_5ms/year_specific_sequence/` | not available |

## Next steps

The analyses below were run on the earlier sequences (`segments_by_song_type.csv`, 20 segments, 6 states) and **need to be redone** with the new 5 ms, 5-state sequences, in this order.

**Sequences**

- [ ] Choose the FASTA version for the alignments: `song_type_sequence` (all years of a song type share one sequence) or `year_specific_sequence` (each taxon uses its own year's recording; 41 of 238 taxa have none and use the representative sequence)

**Alignments**

- [ ] Redo the MAFFT cost optimization for the 5 states (`source/Optimizing_alignment.Rmd`), including the simulated songs and `data/processed/song_segment_lexic.txt`
- [ ] Update the cost matrices, which still include state `m` (`data/processed/mafft_alignments/*_cost_matrix.txt`)
- [ ] Update `source/aligning_song_types.Rmd`: read the new FASTA files, and change `symbols="dfmpsu"` to `symbols="dfpsu"` in the nexus files
- [ ] Rerun the MAFFT and PRANK alignments, and check convergence and gaps (sequences now vary in length: 18 - 38 segments)
- [ ] Regenerate `data/processed/nexus/`

**RevBayes**

- [ ] Change the GTR model from 6 to 5 states, which means 5 stationary frequencies and 10 exchangeability rates (`source/model_GTRG.Rev`, `source/no_fossils/model_GTRG_BD.Rev`)
- [ ] Rerun all models (`source/*.Rev`, `source/trees_with_revbayes.Rmd`), including those with no fossils
- [ ] Rerun the posterior predictions (P3; `source/Write_P3.Rmd`, `source/run_P3_*.sh`)

**Results**

- [ ] Redo the MCMC, ML and P3 diagnostics (`source/Model diagnostics.Rmd`, `source/rwty_diagnostics.Rmd`)
- [ ] Redo the tree topology diagnostics (`source/tree_topology_diagnostics_oct_2024.qmd`)
- [ ] Redo the descriptive statistics (`source/descriptive_stats.Rmd`)
- [ ] Redo the regression models (`source/regression_models.qmd`, `source/song_sequence_similarity.qmd`)
- [ ] Assess the effect of the redundancy of 5 ms sequences (neighbouring segments mostly repeat the same state) on the trees

**Manuscript**

- [ ] Rewrite the methods on sound classification and song coding (now 5 ms segments and 5 states instead of 20 segments and 6 categories), including Fig. 2
- [ ] Replace the repeatability results with the agreement between copies of the same song type, and update the supplementary text (`source/segment_classification_repeatability.qmd`)
- [ ] Redo the figures (`manuscript/Final_Figures.Rmd`) and update all results
- [ ] Revise the discussion, including the assumption on discretizing songs of variable duration

**Website**

- [ ] Add the alignment and RevBayes sections once they are redone

## Website

The website is built with Quarto (`_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`) and deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/publish.yml` on each push to `master`. Code results are read from `_freeze/`, so after editing a report run `quarto render` and commit `_freeze/`.
